app/app/components/PokemonCard.tsx:12-16 — but CardSpecies only carries species id; a real Pokémon-id fix needs widening SpeciesIndex (api.server.ts:86-108) and home's re-mapping (home.tsx:18-20)

changeability.rationale: Rendering fixes land in one obvious component, but loader-level changes hit N copy-pasted blocks, and the absent generated route types make loader↔component edits unsafe rather than merely findable.

coupling.rationale: Server/client separation is clean and enforced by the *.server.ts naming convention; components depend on narrow prop contracts. Docked a point for the any-typed loaderData seam and the Map round-trip in the ability page.

app/app/components/PokemonCard.tsx:27-45 — showTypes/extras props model the real variation between card lists without flag creep
app/app/components/Section.tsx:8-17 — one place for the section/aria-labelledby convention

abstraction_design.rationale: The primitives (cards, sections, badges, sortable table, formatters) stretch well to a new Items resource, but the per-loader dedupe/sort pipeline is copy-paste rather than a shared helper, and home bypasses its own list component.

findings.issue: No route uses the framework's generated Route.LoaderArgs/Route.ComponentProps types (tsconfig is wired for typegen but unused); every component takes loaderData: any and every loader hand-rolls params (move.tsx:9), so loader↔component contract changes compile silently.
findings.suggestion: Import type { Route } from './+types/move' (etc.) and use Route.LoaderArgs / Route.ComponentProps; delete the hand-written parameter and any annotations.

findings.issue: The refs→species dedupe→sort-by-dex block is copy-pasted in three loaders (move.tsx, ability.tsx:14-24, type.tsx:22-29); adding items or changing card order means editing each one.
findings.suggestion: Extract a shared helper in api.server.ts, e.g. refsToSpeciesList(refs: any[]): Promise<SpeciesEntry[]>, and call it from each loader.

findings.issue: Home re-implements the card-grid list markup inline instead of using PokemonCardList, so any card-list change (sorting, markup, classes) needs a second edit here.
findings.suggestion: Render <PokemonCardList species={pageItems} spriteBase={spriteBase} showTypes /> and delete the inline <ul>.

findings.issue: Not-found UI exists twice: the root ErrorBoundary re-implements components/NotFound.tsx (including its title), and each detail route repeats the data({notFound:true},{status:404}) + component branch instead of throwing and letting one boundary render it.
findings.suggestion: throw data(null, { status: 404 }) from loaders, render <NotFound /> from the root ErrorBoundary, and delete the per-route notFound discriminants and branches.

findings.issue: The document-title convention '<h1> – Pokédex' is duplicated in eight files (NotFound.tsx:6, root.tsx:50, home.tsx:111, types.tsx:15, move.tsx:45, ability.tsx:46, type.tsx:55, pokemon.tsx:187) via inline <title> tags rather than a meta export or shared helper.
findings.suggestion: Add a pageTitle(text) helper (or route meta exports) so the suffix and format live in one place.

findings.issue: spriteUrl() is dead code; PokemonCard.tsx:30 builds the identical URL client-side, so the sprite path pattern is known in two places.
findings.suggestion: Either delete spriteUrl() or pass the computed sprite URL per card from loaders so the pattern lives in the server data layer.

findings.issue: The loader flattens per-Pokémon hidden flags into a hiddenBySpecies object that the component re-converts to a Map (ability.tsx:43) — an awkward, double-encoded contract for what is already a per-item boolean.
findings.suggestion: Keep hidden on each item in the pokemon array and render the extra text from it (or compute extras in the loader as a plain list), removing the object→Map round trip.

findings.issue: Section derives the heading id from the title string, so renaming a section title silently changes its aria-labelledby/id (only pokemon.tsx's Moves passes an explicit id).
findings.suggestion: Require (or default to) an explicit id prop and derive the heading id from it, so text changes can't break anchors.

summary: A cleanly layered React Router framework-mode app: server-only data access, pure formatters, small presentational components and presentational props, with the API base URL and caching fully centralized. The big miss is that the framework's generated route types are never used — every component takes any-typed loaderData — so loader↔component edits compile silently, and the per-loader dedupe/sort boilerplate, duplicated NotFound markup and the unused typegen make routine changes more scattered than they need to be. Solid, easy to navigate, but one refactor away from being a codebase you'd point to.
